text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's 1997 public budget will receive 1.4 billion zlotys in privatisation revenues.

- "I'm leaving London with the conviction that Poland is closer than ever to NATO and European Union membership", Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski said following his talks with Britain's Prime Minister John Major.
- More than 100 firms have joined the newly-formed Poland's Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG) Chamber, the chamber's council director Krystyna Nowak said.
- The listed Okocim SA breweries will start producing licensed Carlsberg beer in 1997. Carlsberg holds a controlling stake in Okocim.
- The Norwegian Statoil petroleum concern invested $30 million in its petrol distribution network in Poland this year.
- More than 70 telecoms companies from six countries will exibit their products at the "Komtel'96" international telecommunications fair in Warsaw this November.
- The state-owned PP Porty Lotnicze airport company and Poznan municipality will invest six million zlotys in development of the local Lawica airport in the next two years.

- Poland's Rudport company, controlled by the Huta Katowice steel mill, will construct an iron ore terminal in the Gdansk Polnocny Port by 1999. Its annual reloading capacity will range from six to seven million tonnes.
- Poland's economy has shown the first symptoms of overheating since the second quarter of 1996, the Market Economy Research Institute said.
- Trade unions in the state-owned CPN petrol distribution chain threatened to strike if the government's fuel sector restructuring programme goes ahead.
- Around 56 percent of Poles think the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, serves the country well, a survey by the CBOS polling institute said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland is one of the five countries best prepared for setting up a production base for Japanese companies' west European factories, a Japanese investment forum in Tokyo said.
- Poland's 1997 budget deficit, planned at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), will be financed in a non-inflationary way, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said.
- More than 80 firms are participating in the Olsztyn-based Third Agrofood foodstuffs fair which started yesterday.
- The Olsztyn province governor wants the three towns of Bartoszyce, Szczytno and Dobre Miasto to join the neighbouring Suwalki Special Economic Zone.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Wolczanka shirt maker will contract a brokerage house to manage a several million zloty fund in high risk financial operations this year.
- The listed Farmfood's biggest stakeholder, Conrad Jacobson, has increased its stake to 28.46 percent.
- The state treasury has paid the listed Paged wood processing company 2.4 million zlotys in interest accrued on excess taxes paid in 1989 and 1990.
- Warsaw-based Kredyt Bank has 4.81 percent of votes at the listed Paged annual general meeting (AGM).
PARKIET
- Farmfood has proposed to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) a D-series rights issue offered at 30 to 35 zlotys.

- Slovakia's President Michal Kovacz thanked Poland's Exbud company for the quality, timeliness and professionalism of the construction works carried out in the Bratislava presidential palace, concluded in September this year.

- Credit Lyonnais Securities and Paribas Capital Markets have recently recommended buying the Agros food processor's shares. They stressed the firm's strong market position and good development perspectives.
